paper_title: WebAnything: From the Wild Web to Scalable Agent Environments

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: Web agents require diverse, executable, and resettable website environments for reproducible training and evaluation. Human-assisted mirrors demand per-site engineering, while generative construction can diverge from specified real websites. Capture-and-replay preserves observations, with interaction coverage constrained by captured content and replay capabilities. We present WebAnything, a fully automated framework that reconstructs source-grounded, reusable Web environments from real URLs without per-site manual implementation or repair after initial setup and authorization. An Explorer-Builder collects browser-observable structures, resources, and interaction outcomes; an independent verifier checks frozen candidates and guides local repair or targeted source recapture. We construct 244 website artifacts across 14 application domains and 53 categories, supporting 12,984 executed and accepted tasks. Compared with human-assisted WebHarbor, WebAnything achieves higher aggregate scores on three fidelity metrics, with 12 wins, two ties, and no losses in a blind audit. Fine-tuning Qwen3.5-9B on 5,856 interaction trajectories improves REAL success by 9.9 percentage points, Odysseys-Easy Rubric Avg and Task Avg by 6.25 and 6.32 percentage points, and WebArena-Verified Overall success by 13.33 percentage points under the fixed harness. Code: https://github.com/china-qijizhifeng/Web-Anything

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: Visual Web agents need stable, controllable environments in which they can explore, change state, recover from errors, and receive execution feedback. WebArena and VisualWebArena demonstrate the value of self-hosted websites for reproducible evaluation (Zhou et al., 2024; Koh et al., 2024); WebGym and WebFactory further study scaling environments and interaction experience (Bai et al., 1 2026; Fan et al., 2026). The real Web offers diverse structures and workflows, but live execution complicates state initialization, reproducibility, and safe isolation. We investigate how specified real websites can be automatically transformed at scale into sourcegrounded, executable, and reusable Web agent environments, without requiring manual site-by-site reconstruction. Existing approaches trade off automation, source fidelity, and interaction coverage (Figure 1). Human-assisted mirrors provide controllable, source-corresponding environments but require per-site engineering (WebHarbor Team and Contributors, 2026). Generative methods scale executable sites from specifications and references (Fan et al., 2026; Zhang et al., 2026), but matching specified source remains distinct requirement. Capture-and-replay preserves source observations, with interaction coverage bounded by captured content and replay capabilities (Shi et al., 2017; Srivastava et al., 2026); Weblica combines replay with source-grounded synthesis (Kar et al., 2026). Scaling real-website environments requires both source correspondence and flexible, repeatable interaction. Two technical challenges arise. The SourceGrounding Gap concerns reconstructing structures, resources, and behaviors when private backends and website internals are inaccessible. Screenshots and model priors alone can omit state relationships. Browser observations must instead be organized into evidence that constrains implementation. The Verification and Feedback Gap concerns detecting and correcting reconstruction discrepancies. Builder self-checks can overlook source-inconsistent defects, and discrepancy may reflect either faulty implementation or insufficient observation. These cases require different actions: local repair or additional source capture. We present WEBANYTHING, framework for A. Generative Construction Figure 1: Trade-offs in real-website environment construction. Human-assisted mirrors require per-site engineering; generative methods need source correspondence; replay coverage depends on captured content and replay capabilities. WEBANYTHING combines source-grounded reconstruction, independent verification, and iterative refinement. scalable, source-grounded Web agent environment construction. Starting from real URLs, coupled ExplorerBuilder captures page structures, resources, and before/after interaction observations, then implements executable local routes and state transitions. An Independent Verifier checks frozen candidates in separate context against source evidence and site contracts. Evidence-supported implementation errors trigger local repair; unresolved evidence gaps trigger targeted recapture. Updated candidates are frozen and reverified before release within their declared scope. Fixed initial states, reset mechanisms, and task evaluators support repeated interaction and trajectory collection. Our evaluation covers construction scale, environment quality, and downstream utility. The resource pool contains 244 website artifacts across 14 domains and 53 categories. On five matched WebHarbor sites and 14 historical states, WEBANYTHING achieves higher automated fidelity metrics and 12 wins, two ties, and no losses in blind overall-fidelity audit. Separate interaction tests characterize functional coverage. Historical analysis identifies evidence-supported discrepancies in 39 pairs across 22 sites and independently reverified resolution of 18 issue records across six sites. The environments support 12,984 executed and accepted tasks; SFT on earlier interaction trajectories improves Qwen3.5-9B on REAL, Odysseys-Easy, and WebArena-Verified Overall. Our contributions are: Fully automated, source-grounded reconstruction. We introduce unified Explorer Builder that automatically reconstructs executable Web environments from real URLs, using browser-observable structures, resources, and behaviors without per-site manual implementation or debugging. Independent verification and evidence-aware refinement. An independent verifier checks frozen candidates against source evidence and site contracts, directing discrepancies to local repair or targeted recapture, followed by automated revision and reverification. Scalable environment and task supply. We construct 244 website artifacts across 14 domains, supporting 12,984 executed and accepted tasks. Historical construction records, independent quality evaluations, and downstream SFT demonstrate automation, source fidelity, and practical utility.

sections.title: 2 Related Work
sections.content: Real-Web tasks and executable environments. Mind2Web, WebVoyager, WebGym, WebLINX, SeeAct, Online-Mind2Web, and AssistantBench study tasks or interactions on real websites (Deng et al., 2023; He et al., 2024; Bai et al., 2026; Lù et al., 2024; Zheng et al., 2024a; Xue et al., 2025; Yoran et al., 2024). WebArena, VisualWebArena, REAL, and WebShop emphasize controlled execution and state initialization (Zhou et al., 2024; Koh et al., 2024; Garg et al., 2025; Yao et al., 2022). WorkArena, WorkArena++, and BrowserGym support enterprise workflows and common evaluation 2 infrastructure, while OSWorld and AgentStudio extend executable evaluation to computer environments (Drouin et al., 2024; Boisvert et al., 2024; Le Sellier De Chezelles et al., 2025; Xie et al., 2024; Zheng et al., 2024b). WEBANYTHING connects real-source diversity with repeatable execution by constructing local environments for specified websites. Website generation, replay, and mirroring. WebFactory scales executable sites from specifications and references; InfiniteWeb uses taskcentric test-driven development (Fan et al., 2026; Zhang et al., 2026). VeriEnv provides cloned environments and deterministic SDK-based task verification; WebArena-Infinity iterates generation and testing (Chae et al., 2026a,b; WebArenaInfinity Contributors, 2026). WebGen-Agent combines VLM appearance feedback and GUI testing with backtracking and best-candidate selection for instruction-driven website generation (Lu et al., 2026). Our refinement grounds frozen candidates in URL-specific evidence and routes discrepancies by evidence sufficiency. Screenshot-to-code methods include pix2code, Pix2Struct, WebSight, and Design2Code (Beltramelli, 2017; Lee et al., 2023; Laurençon et al., 2024; Si et al., 2025). World of Bits and WARC-Bench preserve captured content through replay (Shi et al., 2017; Srivastava et al., 2026); Weblica combines replay with sourcegrounded synthesis (Kar et al., 2026). WebHarbor constructs mirrors through humanCoding Agent collaboration (WebHarbor Team and Contributors, 2026). WEBANYTHING jointly uses structural, resource, and behavioral evidence. Separate visual and interaction measurements complement image metrics such as SSIM and LPIPS (Wang et al., 2004; Zhang et al., 2018). Feedback and interaction-data supply. SelfRefine and Reflexion use feedback for output revision and agent reflection (Madaan et al., 2023; Shinn et al., 2023). Our feedback targets frozen website implementations and missing source evidence. AutoGUIWorld synthesizes GUI observations and trajectories, while WEFT studies coordination among environments, tasks, harnesses, and evaluators (Yang et al., 2026; Mao et al., 2026). Synatra and AgentTrek derive demonstrations from indirect knowledge or tutorials; WebRL studies self-evolving task curricula (Ou et al., 2024; Xu et al., 2025; Qi et al., 2025). OS-Atlas, UI-TARS, and OpenCUA expand GUI grounding or interaction data (Wu et al., 2025; Qin et al., 2025; Wang et al., 2025). WEBANYTHING supplies executable environments and collects interaction data with the fixed agent harness and unified task/evaluator pipeline, measuring utility on external benchmarks.

sections.title: 3 Methodology
sections.content: WEBANYTHING uses source evidence as the shared basis for construction and independent verification (Figure 2). An ExplorerBuilder reconstructs executable local pages and states; verification feedback then drives implementation repair or targeted source recapture.

sections.title: 3.2 Source-Grounded Reconstruction
sections.content: State-associated evidence. For each visited state, the ExplorerBuilder associates page structures, computed styles, element geometry, screenshots, and resource references. Actions are linked to subsequent visible feedback and state changes. Distinct interaction states at the same URL remain distinct evidence: closed menu and its expanded state, for example, constrain different implementation requirements. Evidence-constrained implementation. Structural observations constrain layout and component relationships; resource observations ground fonts, images, and media; behavioral observations constrain navigation, filtering, and state modification. The Builder organizes these into local components, 3 Figure 2: WEBANYTHING reconstruction pipeline. Source evidence guides executable construction. Independent checks of frozen candidates drive local repair or targeted recapture; verified candidates are released with repeatable interaction and task-evaluation interfaces. routes, and shared object relationships. Screenshot references thus complement structural and behavioral evidence. specific discrepancy can be traced back to its associated page state and action. When available observations do not establish required outcome, the system seeks additional evidence rather than treating an inferred behavior as observed. Coverage policies. Full Coverage expands accessible page types, interaction states, and neighboring branches from the entry URL and native navigation. Just-in-Time Coverage prioritizes dependencies of given task set and expands them through construction and verification feedback. Both share the reconstruction and acceptance mechanisms, differing in exploration scope and expansion timing. Reported construction experiments use Full Coverage. 3.3 Independent Verification and Evidence-Aware Refinement Verification decoupling. The Builder implements and self-checks candidate; an Independent Verifier then examines the frozen implementation in separate context. It obtains rendering and operation results anew and compares them with source evidence and the site contract. Applicable checks cover pages, controls, resources, workflows, persistence, and restoration. The Verifier cannot edit candidate code. Stateful tests operate through local UI/API interfaces and restore the initial state. Candidate freezing binds findings to the inspected implementation and prevents verification-time repair from changing the target. Evidence-aware refinement. The model diagnoses each discrepancy using check results, source observations, the contract, and runtime conditions. If existing evidence establishes an expected outcome that the candidate fails to reproduce, Local Repair returns the affected page or control, executed action, expected and observed outcomes, and supporting evidence to the Builder. If evidence is insufficient to establish the target outcome, Targeted Recapture forms concrete observation request and revisits the relevant source region. Newly captured structures, resources, or behaviors constrain the next implementation. For example, Figmas authorized source capture established canvas-anchored comment composer. Independent checks found mismatched placement and appearance, providing concrete target for local revision. The Builder read the feedback, changed the editor markup and styles, and submitted new candidate; independent checks then confirmed the composers geometry and visibility. Existing source evidence supported repair in this case; an unresolved observation question instead becomes bounded recapture request (Appendix B.8). After either path updates the candidate, the controller freezes it again and the Verifier repeats affected checks and applicable regression tests. Verification therefore connects discrepancies to actionable revision, while source evidence constrains 4 both initial reconstruction and subsequent refinement. Candidates passing checks within their declared scope can proceed to release. Implementation details and original prompts appear in Appendix B.4.

sections.title: 3.4 Environment and Verifiable Task Supply
sections.content: Released environments package local implementations, resources, initial data, runtime configuration, and reset interfaces. Shared state connects related pages, and applicable creation, modification, and save operations affect later interactions. Fixed initial data and state restoration provide repeatable task starting conditions. The task pipeline generates instructions and matching success conditions for implemented capabilities. Agents execute tasks through fixed browser-based computer-use agent harness shared across data collection and downstream evaluations; settings and execution budgets are specified in Appendix E.1. Evaluators check final answers or terminal environment states. Accepted trajectories are converted into step-level training examples. Task generation, executed acceptance, trajectory collection, and training export remain separate stages and counting units; Section 4.4 reports their outputs.

sections.title: 4 Experiments and Results
sections.content: We study RQ1: construction scale and efficiency, RQ2: environment quality and independent verification, and RQ3: task support and downstream learning utility.

sections.title: 4.1 Experimental Setup
sections.content: Objects and baselines. The resource inventory covers 244 unique website artifacts as of October 9, 2026. Full Coverage construction records for 85 sites support automation and expenditure analysis. Quality comparisons use frozen artifacts and an independent evaluation pipeline: five WebHarbor sites with 14 historical reference states, and five VeriEnv artifacts for offline interaction tests. Historical VeriEnv fidelity references cover four LinkedIn states. Subsets and reference conditions are specified in Appendices A.2A.4. Measurements. Pixel Similarity, SSIM, and Text F1 measure source-state correspondence, aggregated within sites and then averaged equally across sites. blind audit of the 14 WebHarbor-matched states uses final labels agreed through discussion by three annotators, with randomized anonymous mirror order. Interaction tests disable external network access and report capability coverage, executed-test success, and all-test pass, keeping their denominators distinct. Explicit adapters restore initial states. Historical verification analysis links self-checks, independent findings, and repair traces; its definitions appear in Appendix B.7. Tasks and training. Two disjoint collections contain 6,172 accepted tasks across 74 sites and 6,812 across 229 sites. SFT uses earlier WebAnything interaction data: 5,856 trajectories associated with 5,167 unique training task IDs, converted into 60,517 step-level examples. Multiple trajectories or format variants can share task ID. The newer 6,812 tasks are not used in this SFT experiment. We fine-tune Qwen3.5-9B for 473 steps (the fixed training endpoint), with global batch size 256 and learning rate 5 106. Evaluation uses this trained model on REAL (Garg et al., 2025), Odysseys-Easy (Jang et al., 2026), and WebArenaVerified (El hattami et al., 2025); configurations and overlap checks appear in Appendix E.1.

sections.title: 4.2 RQ1: Construction Scale and Efficiency
sections.content: Cross-domain supply. The unified pipeline produces 244 website artifacts across 14 application domains and 53 categories (Figure 3), spanning diverse layouts, navigation structures, and workflows. Artifacts are counted by site identity and recorded homepage availability; deeper fidelity and functionality are assessed separately on evaluated subsets. Appendix F.1 lists the sites, and Appendix A.6 reports additional rendering diagnostics. Automation and recorded expenditure. After initial configuration and necessary authorization, the 85-site historical collection contains no recorded per-site manual implementation, debugging, or repair. Exploration, capture, implementation, and revisions are performed by the pipeline. Recorded model-call cost for 84 sites totals $220.62 (mean $2.63, median $1.60 per site), lower bound that excludes unpriced calls and system overhead. Historical outcomes and accounting details are in Appendix A.1.

sections.title: 5 Conclusion
sections.content: We present WEBANYTHING, an end-to-end automated framework for transforming real websites into source-grounded, executable, and reusable Web agent environments. Unlike human-assisted mirroring approaches, WEBANYTHING automates source exploration, evidence collection, website reconstruction, independent verification, and iterative refinement, eliminating the need for per-site manual implementation and debugging in our audited construction runs. By grounding reconstruction in browser-observable structures, resources, and interaction behaviors, the framework reduces reliance on incomplete visual references or manually specified workflows. Structural, resource, and behavioral evidence guides reconstruction, while independent verification directs discrepancies to local repair or targeted recapture. This separation enables the system to distinguish implementation defects from insufficient source evidence and refine reconstructed environments accordingly. The framework constructs 244 website artifacts across 14 application domains and 53 categories, supporting 12,984 executed and accepted tasks. Experiments demonstrate source fidelity, operational validity, and verification-driven refinement, while also highlighting the importance of evaluating functional coverage independently from visual similarity. Furthermore, supervised fine-tuning on 5,856 interaction trajectories improves Web agent performance on REAL, Odysseys-Easy, and WebArena-Verified, demonstrating the downstream utility of the constructed environments. Together, these results establish practical path toward scaling real-Web agent environments with minimal site-specific human engineering. More broadly, WEBANYTHING connects automated website reconstruction with reproducible interaction and training-data collection, providing foundation for scalable Web agent development and posttraining.

sections.title: Limitations
sections.content: Training validation with large-scale models. Our supervised fine-tuning experiments with Qwen3.5-9B demonstrate the learning value of interaction data from reconstructed environments for downstream Web agent tasks. However, current training experiments primarily concern the 9B parameter scale. We have not systematically evaluated these data with larger foundation models, different post-training methods, or larger training budgets. Future work can examine relationships among environment scale, data diversity, and model capabilities to assess this approach in larger-scale agent training. Continuous real-Web updates and environment maintenance. Real websites continually change their page structures, resources, and interaction behaviors. WEBANYTHING currently reconstructs and verifies source states at particular times, without systematically evaluating the timeliness of local mirrors or long-term maintenance efficiency under continuing source changes. Future research can investigate source-change detection, incremental evidence capture, and local environment updates to reduce maintenance costs while preserving source correspondence. Copyright, content authorization, and environment distribution. High-fidelity reconstruction of real websites involves page content, images, fonts, and branding that may be protected by copyright, trademarks, and terms of service. Public accessibility does not necessarily grant permission to reproduce, modify, or redistribute content. Environment construction, research use, and public release must therefore comply with applicable content authorization and compliance requirements. Future releases can prioritize the general construction framework, evaluation protocols, and de-identified research data, while determining the distribution scope of website mirrors and original resources according to their licenses.

sections.title: Ethical Considerations
sections.content: Exploring, capturing, and reconstructing real websites raises issues concerning terms of service, intellectual property, privacy, and security. The system should process only websites covered by authorization, public licenses, or research agreements, avoid collecting account credentials, cookies, personal information, and payment content, and run released environments in isolated networks and sandboxes. For websites or tasks that could facilitate abusive automation, reconstruction scope, public content, and model capabilities should be restricted.

After initial setup and authorization, this subset contains no recorded per-site manual implementation, debugging, or repair. In the recovered SDK records, the Builder and Verifier primarily used gpt-5.6-sol with xhigh reasoning; some Builder calls used gpt-6-astra, so the entire batch did not use single model. Recovered model-call and partial cost records cover 84/85 sites. sections.title: C Task Supply and Data Statistics
sections.content: C.1 Interfaces for Downstream Task Generation, Evaluation, and Collection Task and training-data construction use released environments. This section describes the implementation interfaces for task specifications, runtime recovery, evaluation, and data binding. From environment capabilities to tasks. The task pipeline reads the pages, visible objects, native operations, and seed data of specific mirror to formulate goals such as retrieval, filtering, detail verification, comparison and aggregation, and state modification. Existing planning materials record whether the required facts reside in lists, detail pages, or other pages, and organize applicable operations into task specifications. Natural-language instructions express user goals, while answers, evidence supporting the operations, and evaluation materials remain hidden. The executable scope of task is bounded by the capabilities and initial state actually supported by the environment. Initial states and success conditions. Public task records contain task identifiers, instructions, sites, starting URLs, and login and reset requirements. Task specifications record capability tags, action and step budgets, and successful and unsuccessful terminal states. Hidden specifications associate required objects, query parameters, source evidence, expected results, and output contracts. Success conditions for information tasks may specify fields, sets, orderings, or comparison results in normalized answers. State-changing tasks check application states after saving, creating, modifying, or restoring objects; tasks admitting multiple solutions use sets of state predicates. When necessary, fictional test records are prepared in private copies of native data structures, while original environment assets remain read-only. Task answers are grounded in the tasks initial data. Task text or nonempty answer file alone does not establish evaluability: corresponding executable checks must exist. Evaluator construction and execution-based verification. During generation, site-specific scripts first check native routes, evidence visibility, and applicable answer, state, and reset conditions. visual agent then receives instructions and observations in the initial state of the corresponding mirror through the fixed harness and performs browser operations. An independent task evaluator checks the final answer against hidden success conditions and determines goal completion using the terminal DOM, screenshots, and applicable state evidence. Model-based evaluation is used for applicable semantic conditions and is separated from agent execution. Tasks with evaluation materials become end-to-end accepted tasks only after actual interaction and outcome checks, rather than receiving pass solely because specifications exist. Recovery, binding, and training entry points. Task execution packages locate native implementations, immutable seeds, and starting routes through runtime descriptions. When login is required, they restore fictional seed identities while isolating real user sessions. Before task execution, mutable databases are restored from seeds, and site-specific reset and startup checks verify applicable states. Tasks whose runtime prerequisites are not met are recorded as blocked. Task identifiers, source-data versions, and specification digests connect public tasks to hidden evaluation materials. Collection packages record implementations, resources, initial data, runtime configurations, and archive digests to associate the complete environment identity. The pipeline separately records task generation, evaluator construction, execution-based acceptance, trajectory collection, and training-sample export. Saved successful trajectories are used for training after quality filtering, format conversion, and step-level sample export. The 6,172 accepted tasks in the earlier source collection, the 5,856 trajectories used for SFT, the 5,167 unique training task IDs obtained by deduplicating task IDs in the training manifest, and the 60,517 step-level samples are counted in their respective units. The relationship between the separate batch of 6,812 new tasks across 229 sites and the 74 source sites follows the set definitions in the experimental setup.
